blocks.text: Strengthen the kid's own sense of accomplishment, and turn it into a positive, empowering moment with their parents.
Age group 6-9 years. 3 types of learners using the app:

Wants to learn: sharing is proof of mastery.
Parents said so: practice becomes pride.
It's a game: the send and the reply feel like a reward round.

Kids share a recording of themselves playing a piece successfully with their parents, and the parents listen and reply in the app. Many parents might never hear their kid play otherwise, so the recording makes it far more likely they will, and their praise reaches the kid soon after the win, while it still means the most. 
**In the future**, these shared moments can become a part of a bigger accomplishment celebration, with a progress timeline, so kids can look back and hear how much they’ve improved.
☝️|In this assignment i covered only the flow of the first run experience of this feature, hence the first time the kid get 3 stars on.
Based on the basic flow we defined together in the whiteboard session. I expanded them to cover more aspects and behaviors of the feature.

Designing for young kids;
  Playful, relatable and celebratory design language. Theme kids know and love.
  Simple messaging
  Voice-over on every screen along with text
  One obvious action per screen
  Multi modal feedback (e.g sound, motion), always positive
The kid is in control, choosing if to send or not
Feature promotion should be subtle to avoid negative sentiment

Parents configured their emails and phone numbers in the app in advance. The uses this details by default.
Recordings are audio only

One message per song share, no multiple songs in one message
One receiver in this version
I didn’t cover them in this assignment.

No parent contact yet: "Ask a grown-up" behind a parent gate.
App is offline: queued, same animation for the kid.
Parent listened, no reply: nothing is shown to the kid.

Multiple receivers.
A sticker notebook (and all messages types) for every completed song.
A weekly digest for parents.
Refined animations and sounds.
Semantic tokens are not defined; Currently tokens (especially colors) are not describing what they should be used for. For example, primary and secondary text colors.
I used Claude text to speech capability for time and resources limitations. For a real product, the voice over should sound MUCH MORE natural, and also friendly, encouraging and excited.
